title: Vector-bundle purity before smooth orientation
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_F$ and uniformizer $\varpi_F$, and $n\geq1$, and put $A=A_{F,n}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $\pi:E\to S$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $d\geq0$ [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. For every $S$-scheme $T$, the finite-level pro-etale Tate sheaf $A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(1)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] has a canonical ordinary-etale descent $A_T^{\mathrm{et}}(1)$ along $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Explicitly, for any $r\geq1$ with $\ell^r A=0$ it is $\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A_T$ [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], canonically independent of $r$, with
$$\nu_T^*A_T^{\mathrm{et}}(1)\cong A_T^{\mathrm{pro}}(1).$$
Use its tensor powers to interpret $A_T(d)$ and $K(d)=K\otimes_A^LA_T(d)$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-kun-derived-tensor]. Use the vector-bundle integration $t_\pi$ of [def-amb-vector-integration], with these coefficient identifications: it is the unique map restricting on each trivializing open to the specified affine-space trace of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], and its bounded coefficient object and map agree with the pro-etale realization under the canonical proper/open site comparisons. For every $K\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the adjoint of
$$
R\pi_!(\pi^*K(d)[2d])
\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}_{\pi,K}^{-1}}K\otimes_A^LR\pi_!A_E(d)[2d]
\xrightarrow{1\otimes t_\pi}K
$$
under the ordinary compact-support adjunction $R\pi_!\dashv\pi^\times$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] is an isomorphism
$$\gamma_{\pi,K}:\pi^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi^\times K.$$
Here $\pi^*$ is exact constant-coefficient inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and $\mathrm{PF}_{\pi,K}$ is the canonical tensor projection map obtained from open extension by zero and the proper projection map [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] on a compactification. No boundedness, constructibility, or finite Tor-amplitude condition is imposed on $K$.

proof.text: Since $\ell\in(\varpi_F)$, we have $\ell^nA=0$; take $m=\ell^n$. Apply [lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent] to every $S$-scheme $T$. It identifies the finite-level pro-etale twist with the inverse image of $\mu_{m,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/m}A_T$, canonically independently of $m$ and compatibly with tensor powers and pullbacks. These are exactly the coefficient identifications in the statement; no freeness of $A$ over $\mathbf Z/m$ is used.

proof.text: Apply [lem-amb-vector-projective-completion] to $E/S$. It gives the compactification $E\xrightarrow{j}\overline E\xrightarrow{r}S$, with $\overline E=\operatorname{Proj}_S\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal O_S\oplus\mathcal E)$, and verifies Noetherianity, finite type and separatedness, including rank zero. Thus [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] supplies the actual ambient right adjoint $\pi^\times$ for the compact-support functor used below.

proof.text:
Put $B_\pi=R\pi_!A_E(d)[2d]$ in the ordinary etale category. The construction in [def-amb-vector-integration] identifies $B_\pi$ with $\mathcal H^0(B_\pi)[0]$ and specifies $t_\pi$ uniquely by its restrictions to trivializing opens. Each restriction is the actual affine-space trace, an isomorphism by [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. Hence the sheaf map $\mathcal H^0(t_\pi)$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-detects-iso], applied to the underlying abelian sheaves. Both complexes have only degree-zero cohomology, so [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] gives that $t_\pi$ is an isomorphism.

For the pro-etale realization, the input $A_E(d)[2d]$ is bounded below. Apply [lem-amb-compact-support-site-comparison-open] to Step 2's compactification and this input. Its specified comparison commutes with open restriction; Step 1 identifies the coefficients. On every trivializing open the pulled-back trace is the same prescribed normalized affine trace. Maps between degree-zero objects are sheaf maps by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful]; the sheaf axiom therefore identifies their global gluings. This identifies the actual named trace on this bounded coefficient input, without asserting an unbounded pro-etale comparison.

proof.text: We spell out the extension-by-zero tensor calculation on the ordinary etale site. For the open immersion $j:E\hookrightarrow\overline E$ of Step 2, $E$ is an object of $\overline E_{\mathrm{et}}$ and the slice site is $E_{\mathrm{et}}$. This $j$ is quasi-compact: its intersection with any affine open of the Noetherian target is a Noetherian open subscheme, hence quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. It is therefore finite type [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type], as required for the extension adjunction used below. The tensor calculation itself applies to any open immersion. For sheaves the natural tensor identity is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor], applied to the constant ring $A_X$. Choose a K-flat resolution $P$ with flat terms of $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], $j^*P$ is a K-flat resolution of $j^*M$. Apply the sheaf identity in every total-tensor degree; direct sums commute with $j_!$ because it is a left adjoint [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Exactness [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] allows this equality to descend through quasi-isomorphisms. It gives $M\otimes_A^L Dj_!L\cong Dj_!(j^*M\otimes_A^LL)$, naturally in arbitrary unbounded $M,L$. Now [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] gives $\pi^\times$ for Step 2's compactification. Apply [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] to $r$, $K$, and $Dj_!A_E(d)[2d]$; the tensor identity just proved changes its target to $R\pi_!(\pi^*K(d)[2d])$. Invert this projection map and follow by $1\otimes t_\pi$, with the actual $t_\pi$ identified in Step 3 and prescribed by [def-amb-vector-integration]. This constructs a global morphism $c_{\pi,K}$ and its adjoint $\gamma_{\pi,K}$.

proof.text: For the affine line $p:\mathbf A^1_T\to T$, put $q:\mathbf P^1_T\to T$ and let $a:\mathbf A^1_T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_T$. The normalized whole-derived-category adjunction $Rq_*\dashv q^*(1)[2]$ of [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] has counit $\epsilon_{q,L}=(1_L\otimes t_q)\pi_q^{-1}$. Compose it with $Da_!\dashv a^*$ from [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Since $Rp_!=Rq_*Da_!$ by [def-amb-etale-compact-support], this constructs $Rp_!\dashv p^*(1)[2]$. Its counit is $\epsilon_{q,L}\circ Rq_*(Da_!a^*q^*L(1)[2]\to q^*L(1)[2])$. Step 4's tensor identification turns the map inside $Rq_*$ into $1_{q^*L}\otimes(Da_!a^*A_{\mathbf P^1_T}(1)[2]\to A_{\mathbf P^1_T}(1)[2])$. Naturality of the canonical proper projection map therefore rewrites this counit as $(1_L\otimes t_p)\pi_p^{-1}$, where $t_p$ is its value at $L=A_T$. The current statement of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] specifies its rank-one adjunction to be exactly this composite of open extension with [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], so its trace is this actual counit at $A_T$. Step 1 identifies this coefficient twist with the finite-level twist of the original integration definition. The twist restriction and the identification of $a^*q^*L(1)[2]$ with $p^*L(1)[2]$ use [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback].

source.place: Step 5(c): projective-line adjunction and restriction to the affine line, with its counit computed

proof.text:
Induct on $e$, with $p_0=1_T$ and identity counit. Step 5 gives the affine-line adjunction and its integration counit. Write $p_{e+1}=p_eh$ with $h:\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf A^e_T}\to\mathbf A^e_T$. The comparison of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] identifies $Rp_{e+1,!}$ with $Rp_{e!}Rh_!$. Compose the adjunctions using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. The right adjoint becomes $h^*(1)[2]p_e^*(e)[2e]=p_{e+1}^*(e+1)[2e+2]$ by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Its counit at $L$ is $\epsilon_{p_e,L}\circ Rp_{e!}(\epsilon_{h,p_e^*L(e)[2e]})$.

Substitute the two integration-counit formulas. The composition identity in [lem-amb-shriek-tensor-composition] combines their projection maps, including the proper/open interchange. The resulting counit is $(1_L\otimes t_{p_{e+1}})\mathrm{PF}_{p_{e+1},L}^{-1}$. To identify its trace, evaluate the ordered composite counit at $A_T$: this is the definition in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. Each intermediate coefficient value is a shifted Tate sheaf by that node's trace isomorphism and Step 4's projection formula, hence bounded below. The bounded-below agreement in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] identifies precisely the two composition maps on these values. Thus this is the specified actual trace.

The adjunct of this counit under any chosen right adjoint is an isomorphism: the two adjunction Hom bijections give mutually inverse comparisons by applying each to the other's counit. Therefore the normalized affine-space comparison is invertible for every unbounded $L$.

proof.text:
Choose an affine Zariski cover $u:U\hookrightarrow S$ trivializing $\mathcal E$, and put $v:E_U\hookrightarrow E$, $\pi_U:E_U\to U$. The opens $U$ and $E_U$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Applying the same statement to their intersections with affine opens of their targets shows that $u,v$ are quasi-compact; hence they are of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. An open immersion is locally an identity map, so is etale; its diagonal is an isomorphism, hence it is separated. For arbitrary $M\in D(E_U,A)$, the composition isomorphisms of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], the equality $\pi v=u\pi_U$, and the normalization [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization] for $u,v$ give
$$R\pi_!Dv_!M\cong R(\pi v)_!M=R(u\pi_U)_!M\cong Du_!R\pi_{U!}M.$$
Apply the exact etale-extension adjunctions of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], the global adjunction, and the adjunction for $\pi_U$ from [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Their Hom bijections give, naturally in $M$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{E_U}(M,v^*\pi^\times K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{S}(R\pi_!Dv_!M,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{U}(R\pi_{U!}M,u^*K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{E_U}(M,\pi_U^\times u^*K).$$
Take the images of the two identity maps to obtain inverse maps between the represented objects; naturality makes both composites identities. This supplies the canonical isomorphism $\beta_K:v^*\pi^\times K\cong\pi_U^\times u^*K$. In particular we have derived base restriction using both extension adjunctions and compact-support composition; we have not applied the domain-only locality lemma as if it asserted base restriction.

source.place: Step 7: the identity u prime inverse image R pi ! = R pi_U ! u inverse image, proved by explicit Hom adjunctions

proof.text:
Use the canonical exchange $C:u^*R\pi_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi_{U!}v^*$ of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. The twist pullback formulas of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] identify $v^*(\pi^*K(d)[2d])$ with $\pi_U^*(u^*K)(d)[2d]$. By [def-amb-vector-integration] and Step 3, $u^*t_\pi=t_{\pi_U}$ under this coefficient exchange. Apply [lem-amb-shriek-projection-open-restriction] to $f=\pi$, $M=A_E(d)[2d]$ and $K$. It identifies the actual projection maps and their inverses after restriction. Consequently the restricted integration counit $u^*c_{\pi,K}$ is $c_{\pi_U,u^*K}$ under $C$.

The Hom chain of Step 7 uses the extension/composition comparison $\delta:R\pi_!Dv_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Du_!R\pi_{U!}$. By [lem-amb-shriek-open-exchange-adjoint], its pairing with the evaluation counits has adjunct exactly $C^{-1}$. Thus taking adjuncts of the preceding equality uses the same exchange as that Hom chain and yields
$$\beta_K\circ v^*\gamma_{\pi,K}=\gamma_{\pi_U,u^*K}.$$
Indeed both sides transpose to the same restricted integration counit through these adjunction bijections. On the chosen trivialization $E_U=\mathbf A^d_U$, Step 6 proves the right side invertible. Step 7 makes $\beta_K$ an isomorphism, so $v^*\gamma_{\pi,K}$ is an isomorphism on each such open.

proof.text: For every integer $n$, exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] commutes with $\ker d/\operatorname{im}d$, so it identifies $v^*\mathcal H^n(\gamma_{\pi,K})$ with $\mathcal H^n(v^*\gamma_{\pi,K})$. By Step 8 this is an isomorphism on each member $E_U$ of an open cover of $E$. Every geometric point of $E$ lies in one of these opens; its stalk is the same stalk computed there. Thus [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] makes every $\mathcal H^n(\gamma_{\pi,K})$ an isomorphism. The unbounded cohomology criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], applied to the abelian category of etale $A$-module sheaves, now proves that $\gamma_{\pi,K}$ itself is an isomorphism. No gluing or equality detection for arbitrary derived morphisms is asserted: the global mate was constructed in Step 4, its local equality was proved by adjunction in Step 8, and only its isomorphy is detected locally.
